title: Health
description: Words for topics on public health, diet, exercise, healthcare systems and mental wellbeing.

words.definition: involving a lot of sitting and little physical activity
words.example: A sedentary lifestyle increases the risk of heart disease and diabetes.

words.definition: the condition of being very overweight in a way that is dangerous to health
words.example: Childhood obesity has doubled in many countries over the last twenty years.

words.definition: intended to stop illness or a problem before it happens
words.example: Investing in preventive healthcare can save governments money in the long term.

words.definition: the average number of years a person is expected to live
words.example: Life expectancy has risen steadily thanks to better sanitation and vaccines.

words.definition: lasting for a long time or happening repeatedly
words.example: Chronic diseases such as diabetes place a heavy burden on hospitals.

words.definition: a large number of cases of a disease in one area at the same time
words.example: Some experts describe the rise in diabetes as a silent epidemic.

words.definition: containing substances that help the body grow and stay healthy
words.example: Schools should provide nutritious meals rather than processed snacks.

words.definition: food changed by industrial methods, often with added salt, sugar or fat
words.example: Diets high in processed food are linked to a range of health problems.

words.definition: the state of being healthy, happy and comfortable
words.example: Regular contact with nature has a positive effect on mental wellbeing.

words.definition: giving a substance to protect people from a disease
words.example: Mass vaccination programmes have almost eliminated polio worldwide.

words.definition: identifying what illness a person has
words.example: Early diagnosis greatly improves the chances of surviving cancer.

words.definition: systems for clean water and the removal of waste to protect health
words.example: Poor sanitation remains a major cause of disease in some rural communities.

words.definition: caused by worry or pressure
words.example: Long working hours are a leading cause of stress-related illness.

words.definition: extreme tiredness caused by working too hard for too long
words.example: Many nurses suffer from burnout after years of night shifts.

words.definition: a period of physical exercise
words.example: Even a short daily workout can improve your mood and energy.

words.definition: to become healthy again after an illness or injury
words.example: Patients tend to recover more quickly when they have family support.

words.definition: a sign of an illness
words.example: Fatigue and headaches are common symptoms of dehydration.

words.definition: able to spread from person to person
words.example: Measles is one of the most contagious diseases known.

words.definition: the services that provide medical care
words.example: Universal healthcare ensures that treatment does not depend on income.

words.definition: poor health caused by not eating enough or not eating the right food
words.example: Malnutrition in early childhood can affect brain development.

words.definition: a child's growth being limited by poor nutrition
words.example: Reducing stunting has become a national priority in Indonesia.

words.definition: the quality of not doing something too much
words.example: Sugar is not harmful if it is eaten in moderation.

words.definition: causing harm or damage
words.example: Lack of sleep has a detrimental effect on concentration.

words.definition: a patient who receives treatment at a hospital without staying overnight
words.example: Many minor operations are now carried out on outpatients.

words.definition: the body's system for fighting infection and disease
words.example: A balanced diet helps to strengthen the immune system.

words.definition: the inability to stop doing or using something harmful
words.example: Nicotine addiction is extremely difficult to overcome without support.

words.definition: to make pain or a problem less severe
words.example: Gentle exercise can alleviate the symptoms of back pain.

words.definition: a population in which the proportion of older people is increasing
words.example: An ageing population will put growing pressure on health budgets.
collocations: the challenges of an ageing population

words.definition: a person's emotional and psychological condition
words.example: Schools are beginning to take students' mental health more seriously.

words.definition: an unwanted effect of a drug or treatment
words.example: Drowsiness is a common side effect of some allergy medicines.
